name: KY-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 Louisville-based district fundamentals favor Democrats
Incumbent McGarvey holds a large cash advantage ($1.8M on hand) over a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
No public polling or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A double-digit Democratic lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with no visible financial support all point to a Safe Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 97%. With no polling available, the margin estimate leans on district fundamentals and candidate resources.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against McGarvey or a strongly favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, though flipping a D+10 seat remains a tall order.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 3rd District, anchored in Louisville, leans Democratic by about ten points and has been held by Morgan McGarvey since 2023. McGarvey is seeking another term and has built a substantial financial lead, raising roughly $1.6 million and holding $1.8 million on hand. Republican nominee Maria Rodriquez shows no significant fundraising in the available record, and no outside spending on either side appears in the data.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 97%. With a double-digit partisan lean, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced challenger, the seat is rated Safe Democratic. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves room for a smaller-than-expected margin even though the outcome rarely appears in doubt.
